findings.title: Escaped YAML values evade restored handoff privacy checks
findings.why_it_matters: The restored scan checks raw YAML rather than its decoded values. Valid noncanonical handoff frontmatter can therefore contain an email or configured private term that the previous validation path rejected, while both --path and --changed now accept it. R1 is fixed for literal values, but the previous frontmatter privacy protection is not fully preserved.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the raw scan and additionally scan decoded/reserialized frontmatter when it parses successfully, using the existing scanPersonalData rules. Do not introduce baton-schema validation for noncanonical documents. Verify escaped emails and configured terms across all three documentation paths and both selectors, retaining allowed inline body examples.
evidence: Trigger: write valid frontmatter containing description: "person\u0040private.example" to .specify/extensions/baton/commands/handoff.md, baton/templates/handoff.md, or baton/speckit-extension/commands/handoff.md.

Previously, validate called validateHandoff(root, path) without a source argument. src/lib/handoff.mjs parsed YAML and scanned serializeFrontmatter(data, '') with frontmatter: true. The decoded description is person@private.example, which produces E_DENYLIST.

The new branch at lines 173–179 extracts and scans the original YAML bytes. The raw value contains no literal @, so scanPersonalData returns no privacy error. Neither the selected-path follow-up scan nor the changed-file follow-up scan restores decoded-value inspection; selected-path scanning skips handoff.md, and changed-file scanning either excludes .specify or scans raw text.
A read-only, in-memory execution of the exact new branch returned [] for this input, while the previous parsed/reserialized scan returned E_DENYLIST.

The same verification used description: "private\u002downer-term" with configured term private-owner-term: YAML decoding produced that private term, the previous scan rejected it, and the new branch returned [].
